title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. No weights are trained (the policy is frozen Claude Opus 4.8). The 'training signal' is a finite evolve set reused adaptively across rounds: Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks, unit-test verified) for coding; Harvey LAB (160 legal tasks, fixed split into 120 evolve and 40 ID held-out, each graded by 20-100 per-criterion LLM-judge verdicts, about 14,000 verdicts per evaluation) for agentic workspace; and 61 license-free EngDesign tasks graded by frozen simulators. OOD held-out suites are SWE-bench Verified, JobBench, GDPval (185 tasks, 3-judge majority vote vs human experts), APEX-Agents (480 tasks, pass@1) and Frontier-Eng (47-task v1 Medal Score, 38 buildable). A noise band delta is measured beforehand from repeated runs of the unchanged base harness.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Instead of staged training, RRSI runs T rounds of harness evolution (T=20 for coding and agentic workspace, 40 for engineering design; k=2 or 4 trials per task) with a cosine-annealed edit budget b_t = b_min + (b_max - b_min) * 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi*t/T)), decaying from b_max=3-4 to b_min=1. Early rounds therefore allow coordinated multi-edit candidates, and late rounds allow only single attributable edits. A stall detector (window w=3) reserves m_draft=1 of 2 candidate slots for never-exercised components when progress stays within delta.
method: RRSI keeps the harness edit space open (prompts, control flow, config, output plumbing, context management, client tools, skills, memory, subagents) and instead regularizes the search trajectory. Proposal side: an L0-style cap on independently attributable edits per candidate drawn from an 80-edit pool; evidence-aware credit assignment that logs component, hypothesis, diff, score and cost change, and acceptance for every edit; and structured exploration on stalls. Selection side: a leakage critic reads each diff before evaluation and rejects task names, answers and benchmark-specific logic; a noise-adjusted floor requires S(H') >= S* - delta; Ridge/L2-style complexity-aware acceptance requires relative token growth dC <= beta0 + beta1*dS when dS > delta (beta0=0.10-0.15, beta1=24.4-44.5), with a shaped within-band rule w_s*dS - w_c*dC + w_n*novelty > 0; and Lasso/L1-style pruning flags components with no positive gain over n_prune=4-5 rounds as deletion targets. Proposer, analyst and critic are all Claude Opus 4.8.
eval_metrics: Benchmarks: Terminal-Bench 2.1 accuracy and SWE-bench Verified resolve rate (coding); Harvey LAB criteria pass rate, JobBench weighted rubric, GDPval win rate vs experts, and APEX-Agents pass@1 (agentic workspace); EngDesign pass rate and Frontier-Eng Medal Score (engineering design). Cost is measured in policy tokens per trial and steps per trial. Baselines are H0, Meta-Harness, AHE, TTHE and HarnessX under the same candidate budget. Gains over H0: TB2.1 74.2->80.2, SWE-V 82.0->83.8, Harvey evolve 89.4->90.5, Harvey held-out 86.9->89.2, JobBench 36.0->40.7, GDPval 48.8->52.3, APEX 34.2->37.9, EngDesign 50.0->54.9, Frontier-Eng 17.7->22.0. Reliability is assessed with paired task-level bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples, all excluding zero) and an independent rerun of every search, which agrees within 1.8 points.
key_results: RRSI gains up to 6.0 points on the evolve split and improves every held-out split, by up to 4.3 OOD (Frontier-Eng +4.3 Medal, +24.3% relative). The agentic OOD average is 43.6 vs 39.7 for H0 and at most 40.6 for prior methods; AHE and TTHE end below H0. The final harness uses 2.42M tokens/trial vs 3.80M for unregularized evolution; removing all regularizers raises the evolve score to 92.8 but drops the OOD average to 40.3.
evolution_note: RRSI responds to the 2026 wave of automated harness evolution (Meta-Harness, AHE, TTHE, HarnessX, Self-Harness, Darwin Godel Machine-style self-modification) and to evidence that their evolve-set gains often fail to transfer. It reframes harness RSI as adaptive empirical optimization on a reused finite evolve set (citing Dwork et al. on adaptive data analysis) and imports classical L0/L1/L2 regularization, noise-aware acceptance and leakage screening into the search. Harness transfer becomes the evaluation criterion: harnesses evolved on one suite carry over to unseen benchmarks and to backbones never used in the search (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite).
